For decades, one of Kyrgyzstan's greatest economic challenges has been the steady outflow of workers. Hundreds of thousands of Kyrgyz citizens have left to seek employment abroad, particularly in Russia, sending home remittances that account for a substantial share of the country's economy. While those transfers support many families, they also leave Kyrgyzstan dependent on foreign labor markets and vulnerable to demographic decline.
To address that challenge, the Kyrgyz government has continued encouraging members of the ethnic Kyrgyz diaspora to return. According to the Ministry of Labor, Social Security and Migration, 387 ethnic Kyrgyz received returnee (kairylman) status during the first seven months of 2026.

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE — AUG 15 ⚡

☢️ #Uranium | 🟠 #Copper | 🥈 #Silver | 🥇 #Gold

Four metals. One pulse. No noise.

Markets are closed. The signals are not.

☢️ URANIUM — ONE DECISION, MORE DEMAND

Spain has extended both Almaraz reactors until June 2030, keeping roughly 2 GW of nuclear capacity online.

Compared with the previous closure schedule, the extension implies approximately 2 million pounds of additional U₃O₈ demand.

A political decision can add demand to the forecast overnight.

New uranium supply still takes years.

🟠 COPPER — THE LME SQUEEZE INTENSIFIES

LME cash copper reached a record $14,545/t on Friday—$411 above the three-month contract.

Inventories fell 8% in one week to 204,975 tonnes.

Copper exists, but increasingly not where buyers need it. Bullish near term.

🥈 SILVER — MACRO SUPPORT RETURNS

Silver closed just below $65/oz, gaining approximately 2.6% for the week.

Weak US retail sales reduced expectations of a September Fed hike. Citi continues to target $75/oz over 0–3 months and $90 over 6–12 months.

🥇 GOLD — STRATEGIC BUYERS KEEP ACCUMULATING

Gold finished near $4,380/oz as the dollar weakened and rate-hike expectations declined.

Central banks bought 289 tonnes in Q2, while Tether acquired 27.1 tonnes during H1.

Gold accumulation is no longer solely a central-bank story.

Gavin Baker: AI is too dangerous to centralize

@GavinSBaker:

“I think Anthropic and people in the effective altruism movement believe that this technology is too dangerous to distribute.

And what Mark Zuckerberg and I think Elon and Jensen believe is that this technology is too dangerous to centralize.

And history has spoken, and when given the choice, it is always better to distribute and decentralize.

There's really no counter example that I can think of. And just forget as an American, but as a human, I want an AI that looks out for me, and my conception of what's good for America.

I do not want Dario Amodei or Anthropic deciding what's in my best interests. I just fundamentally don't want that.”

Jason:

“You don't trust AI Jesus?”

Gavin:

“He seems like a great guy, you know? Although it is funny, somebody said he was cursed with resting smiling face, and it is a little weird to listen to him talk about this terrible vision for humanity while he's smiling happily.”

Did a lot of reading and thinking re: Where we go from here in the AI cycle over the weekend. 

On this website there exists a class of AI substack bros who have become very rich from being right on AI, and thus they have become the default signal for anything AI related. These guys bought Sandisk at $100, Neoclouds 50% cheaper, Bottlenecks before they ran up, and have YTDs of 10-20x. 

Given that SNDK was only at 200 at the start of this year, yea we had some magnificent gains. Now the next question to me is: Now What? Where will the next big trade come from?

My first instinct is that I am fitting a square peg into a round hole. These things tend to be obvious, and the fact that I have obsessed over this question over and over in the past few weeks is a red flag. AI was obvious at the start of the year, and hence it made money. So was crypto in 2024 when Trump got elected and we had a bull market.

But now, trying to "figure it out", is actually not a good sign. It's akin to trying to "buy crypto assets" in 2026 - you have to do so much logical convincing that these are good buys instead of facing the truth. 

And I can see it in my writing. I wrote to my subscribers a couple of days ago that these are just trading assets now. And yea the obvious easy bearish argument is that earnings are real, AI is real, and they will keep going up. I don't doubt that AI is real, earnings are real. But it's the consequence I doubt - that the prices of these assets can just keep going up ad infinitum when everyone knows that they are in need of compute and short of memory. 

My bread and butter have been asymmetric opportunities, which can be boiled down to one intuition - does it have good risk-reward? 

I think right now there's only 3 playing fields in the AI trade that offer good risk/reward

1. Buying microcaps that turn out to be strong competitors. 

2. Buying companies that become eventual monopolies / have a large stake, and aren't priced that way right now - Neoclouds are 

3. Buying new frontier-tech derived trades. Like if tomorrow someone says they want speed and CBRS just re-rates upwards 10x - that sort of trades.

tweets.text:
If you were in San Francisco during the crypto token boom, the AI token boom feels weirdly familiar, especially at the extremes.

Extreme displays of wealth. This constant paranoia that you need to make generational money right now or somehow you’ll end up poor. Everyone around you seems to be getting richer, so even if you’re doing objectively well, you start feeling like you’re the only idiot missing the trade haha

Then come the shady deals, insiders making absurd money, people optimizing every relationship for upside, very little loyalty, and a surprising amount of betrayal the second incentives change.

It creates this strange atmosphere where ambition, FOMO, greed and genuine technological excitement are all mixed together.

The huge difference is that AI is actually an extraordinary underlying technology. The economic value being created is real, the productivity gains are real, and the benefit to humanity is enormous!!

So from my experience, the boom can feel unhealthy at the edges while the thing we’re collectively building is incredibly healthy and important.
